question: Application of the mutual assistance clause under Article 42(7) TEU in the event of an attack against a Member State

Under Article 42(7) of the Treaty on European Union, if a Member State is the victim of armed aggression on its territory, the other Member States are obliged to provide aid or assistance using every means at their disposal.

This provision is especially important in light of the ongoing tensions in the Eastern Mediterranean and the need to ensure the territorial integrity and sovereignty of all Member States of the Union. Given that the Republic of Cyprus and Greece are both Members of the European Union, can the Commission answer the following: 1.
In the event of armed aggression by Türkiye against the territory of the Republic of Cyprus or Greece, would the mutual assistance clause of Article 42(7) TEU be automatically triggered?
What specific obligations does this provision entail in practice for the remaining Member States and what is the role of the EU institutions in its implementation?
